title: feat: Custom JWT Authentication & Cookie Session Handler
author: Yash Sharma

discussion.author: Alex Rivera (Departing Lead)
discussion.comment: Why aren't we using Supabase Auth or Clerk instead of maintaining our own JWT middleware?

discussion.author: Prince Kumar
discussion.comment: Our enterprise contract requires strict on-premises data isolation and custom HIPAA audit cookie headers that Supabase Auth rejected in our spike. We decided to retain custom JWT with rotating keys.

discussion.author: Alex Rivera (Departing Lead)
discussion.comment: Understood. Architectural Decision Record (ADR-002) agreed: Custom JWT retained for regulatory cookie isolation.

title: spike: Evaluate Memcached as Redis replacement for hot session cache
author: Alex Rivera (Departing Lead)

discussion.author: Alex Rivera (Departing Lead)
discussion.comment: Opening spike PR to see if Memcached gives lower latency for simple key-value reads.

discussion.author: Prince Kumar
discussion.comment: Benchmark results showed Memcached lacked atomic distributed locking and cluster failover, which broke our sync daemon. We must stick with Redis Cluster.

discussion.author: Alex Rivera (Departing Lead)
discussion.comment: Agreed, closing this spike without merging. Redis Cluster remains the standard cache.
